overview.text: The Scarlet Kingsnake is a small, harmless kingsnake of the south-eastern United States. Its red, black and yellow bands copy the venomous coral snake.

identification.text: Bands of red, black and white or yellow - like a coral snake, which may protect it from predators.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: The south-eastern USA from Virginia and Kentucky south to Florida and west to Mississippi.

habitat.text: Pine flatwoods, hammocks, pine savannas, pine-oak forests, prairies, fields and suburbs - it even turns up in swimming pools.

diet.text: A specialist: mostly lizards, nearly all skinks - the narrowest diet of any kingsnake.

reproduction.text: Mates in late May and early June and lays eggs in June and July, which hatch after 40 to 65 days.

recognise.text: Red, black and yellow or white bands.
